title: 20251208 - You don't have to make Test Plans anymore...

chapters.title: Presenter introduction: Tina Starridge and project overview
What is a test plan and why it matters
Benefits of test plans and scenario types
Scenario IDs, descriptions, and test types
Challenges of manual test plan creation
Introduction to AI-assisted test plan generation and structured prompts

features.name: AI-assisted test plan generation
features.description: Using AI and system prompts to generate test plans from requirements automatically, creating a starting point for testers. AI agents can generate test plans from requirements, creating scenarios with user actions and outcomes that can be iteratively refined through prompt adjustments based on expert feedback.
caveats: Project started over a year ago as an exploratory collaboration
AI output is not perfect and requires review by testers
Quality depends on input user story clarity
Initial output may include unnecessary details

features.name: Test plan methodology at 4PS
features.description: A structured approach to creating test plans by listing user scenarios from requirements before coding, used to validate requirements and improve software quality.
caveats: Based on manual work currently
Example provided is not a very large test plan

features.name: User scenario classification
features.description: Classification of test scenarios into sunny-path (positive) and rainy-path (negative) scenarios to ensure comprehensive testing coverage.
caveats: AI assistance with marking positive and negative scenarios mentioned as challenging

features.name: Structured system prompts for test planning
features.description: Framework using five components for AI prompts - instructions, steps, format requirements, examples, and notes - to generate consistent and structured test plans from requirements.
caveats: Requires understanding of prompt engineering principles
Approach evolved and changed over twelve months

features.name: MCP integration for test planning in Visual Studio Code
features.description: Using Model Context Protocol (MCP) within Visual Studio Code to connect requirements from Azure DevOps directly to AI language models for generating test plans. MCP servers act as toolboxes that can be given to AI agents to connect to external systems like Azure DevOps.
caveats: Language models cannot natively connect to external systems like Azure DevOps without MCP
Requires testers to learn Visual Studio Code
Requires proper tool configuration in VS Code

features.name: System prompts in VS Code for structured test plan generation
features.description: Users can create system prompt files in VS Code that specify instructions for AI to follow when generating test plans. These prompts can be invoked with slash commands like /create test plan and can include access to tools like Azure DevOps.
caveats: Initial prompt quality may be poor without proper structure
Requires iterative refinement to achieve good results

features.name: AI-assisted prompt generation and refinement
features.description: Users can ask AI to help create better system prompts by describing what components should be included like instructions, steps, format requirements, examples, and notes. This creates a dialogue where users can iteratively refine prompts.
caveats: First iteration is often suboptimal
Requires back-and-forth dialogue to sharpen

features.name: AI-structured requirement analysis into test scenarios
features.description: AI can organize unstructured requirements into structured test plans with positive paths, negative paths, test scenarios, and examples. Quality depends on the quality of the input requirement.
caveats: AI may make up content if requirements lack detail
Output quality depends on input requirement quality

features.name: Expert feedback loop for test plan improvement
features.description: Domain experts can provide feedback on AI-generated test plans to refine system prompts. This iterative loop transforms vague AI responses into structured, production-ready test plans with proper wording, priority levels, and detail granularity.
caveats: Requires domain expert involvement
Multiple iterations needed to achieve production quality

features.name: Prompt-based slash commands for AI tasks
features.description: Users can execute pre-configured AI prompts via slash commands (e.g. /create test plan, /review pull request) without needing to be prompt engineers, enabling non-technical roles to leverage AI.
caveats: Requires pre-configured prompts to be set up
Non-technical users can execute but not create prompts

features.name: Multi-use case AI prompts
features.description: AI prompts can be created for various non-coding tasks beyond test planning, including requirements formulation, clarifying questions, documentation from pull requests, pull request reviews, and translation reviews.
caveats: Different prompts needed for different tasks
Requires centralized management for team/company

features.name: AI as junior developer paradigm
features.description: Approach treating AI as a junior developer that needs clear instructions and iterative feedback. First attempts will be messy but improve through iteration as instructions are refined based on team and organizational preferences.
caveats: Requires multiple iterations
Dependent on quality of initial instructions

features.name: AI reduces manual test planning effort
features.description: AI can significantly speed up test plan creation by generating first drafts in minimal time, reducing manual effort and allowing teams to focus on refinement and optimization rather than starting from scratch.
caveats: Does not replace human expertise
Quality dependent on user story completeness

features.name: Centralized prompt management for teams
features.description: Capability to create and manage standardized prompts (e.g. create test plan) for a company or team, maintained by a designated team, which other team members can execute via slash commands without modification.
caveats: Requires central team to manage and maintain prompts
Company-wide standardization may limit customization

features.name: VS Code extension for prompt distribution
features.description: A VS Code extension that automatically downloads and updates prompt files to user directories, checking repositories for newer versions whenever VS Code opens and distributing them across the organization.
caveats: still in planning phase
implementation with simple prompts

features.name: Phased prompt deployment strategy
features.description: A three-stage rollout approach: keeping prompts inside projects initially, then moving to user settings for accessibility across projects, and finally centralizing updates via VS Code extensions.
caveats: requires organizational buy-in
depends on user comfort with AI tooling
